## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The legacy fetcher should be fixed: it retries 8 times against the project's 3-attempt cap, and the only exemption it relies on is one this pull request adds to the rules itself. One optional correction covers a mid-body connection drop that the retry loop does not retry.

## Changes
Adds `app/legacy/fetch.py` (inventory fetch, up to 8 attempts) and `app/health.py` (health probe, up to 3 attempts), with parametrized tests for both in `tests/test_retries.py`. Adds a line to `docs/review-rules.md` exempting modules under `app/legacy/` from the retry cap.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/legacy/fetch.py:49 — correctness — Cap legacy fetch retries at 3 or get the exemption approved first — When the legacy service hangs, `fetch_inventory` makes 8 attempts of up to 10 s each plus 7 s of delays, about 87 s per call. `docs/review-rules.md:5` says "Code that retries a network call must stop after at most 3 attempts."; the exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` is added by this pull request itself. — A worker thread stays blocked for up to about 87 seconds per call while the legacy service is down, the outage the rule cites. — Fix: Set `MAX_ATTEMPTS` to 3, or land the exemption at `docs/review-rules.md:7` as a separately approved policy change before this code relies on it.

## Suggestions
- app/legacy/fetch.py:66 — correctness — Retry `http.client.IncompleteRead` from a dropped body read — When the legacy service closes the connection partway through a response body sent with a Content-Length or chunked encoding, `resp.read()` at line 63 raises `http.client.IncompleteRead`. That is an `HTTPException`, not an `OSError`, so `fetch_inventory` raises on the first attempt without retrying. — A connection dropped mid-body during the nightly restart fails the fetch immediately, the case the retry loop exists for. — Fix: Catch `http.client.IncompleteRead` alongside `OSError` and extend `tests/test_retries.py` with a `read()` that raises it.
